    Positive filtered deformations #

    Definition 6.2 (def:positive-deformation, positive-deformations.tex): "A positive filtered deformation of a finite-dimensional nonnegatively graded algebra Λ is an algebra B with a finite decreasing multiplicative filtration and an identification gr B = Λ." The identification is recorded by the leading-term maps σ_d : F^d → Λ_d (PosFiltration), surjective with kernel F^{d+1} and multiplicative.

    Lemma 6.4 (lem:split-positive-deformation, lines 189–233): the vertex idempotents lift (through the nilpotent ideal F¹), and the filtration splits as S-bimodules, giving a linear isomorphism φ : Λ ≅ B that is an S-bimodule map, sends Λ_{≥d} onto F^d and has leading term the identity (exists_split). In the transported multiplication a ⋆ b = φ⁻¹(φa φb) the S-actions are those of Λ and a ⋆ b - ab raises degree (star_sub_mul_ge).

    Here the splitting is built from diagonal idempotents whose degree-0 corners are lines (Diag, exists_splitD); for S = Λ₀ ≅ kⁿ (Vertices) this is exists_split. A split semisimple S with matrix blocks is handled in Refinements/SplitSemisimple.lean by lifting matrix units and transporting the splitting of the root corners.
